newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Cheques ready for work-to-rule Nigerian oil staff.
newsitem.headline: Cheques ready for work-to-rule Nigerian oil staff.

text.p: Pay cheques are now ready for staff at Nigeria's Department of Petroleum Resources (DPR) who have been on work-to-rule since Monday over non-payment of salaries, a spokeswoman for the department said on Thursday.
DPR processes export documents for Nigerian oil shipments and its staff have been going to their offices but not working to back for the payment of salaries.
"We have collected the cheques for the payment of workers' salaries and arrears from the petroleum ministry," spokeswoman Belema Oshibodu told Reuters.
She said the cheques were collected last weekend after the finance ministry released the second quarter funding allocation to the petroleum ministry.

Victor Ajakaye, chairman of the DPR chapter of the white-collar oil workers' union PENGASSAN, told Reuters on Tuesday that his members were going to work but were not working until their demands were met.
The work-to-rule action followed the expiration last Friday of the workers' ultimatum to the oil ministry.
Ajakaye said salary arrears and other benefits owed the 3,000-strong DPR staff amounted to 300 million naira.
"The DPR is not unmindful of the various workers demand and the issues are being addressed," Oshibodu said.
DPR staff are responsible for processing documents before crude oil is lifted from Nigerian terminals.
In February they threatened to go on strike over non-payment of salaries but called it off after part of the wages was paid.
Oil industry sources said the work-to-rule action was capable of slowing processing of exports if it was not checked.
The workers union officers were away in midwestern Benin City attending an oil conference and could not be reached to say when the work-to-rule action would be called off.
